nodes.title: SG-4 · Add Git-backed contribution storage and API
nodes.body:
Context: backend has only player sessions and /healthz. Desired behavior: a contribution service validates and stores each idea as an immutable Markdown file in Git under worlds/the-boys-room/rounds/<round>/contributions/, exposed through world and contribution endpoints. Expected result: players submit ideas safely and concurrently. Why: Git is the single source of truth.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given an OPEN round, when a valid prompt is POSTed, then a unique Markdown file is written and committed with the bot identity
- Given invalid input (length, world, status, limit, rate, duplicate), when submitted, then the request is rejected with a 4xx status and no file is written
- Given concurrent submissions, when they run together, then each produces a distinct file
- Given a traversal path segment, when used, then it is rejected
- All seven listed endpoints respond from the service/world repository


## Scope
- In scope: backend/internal contribution service, git wrapper, world repository, handlers, wiring
- Out of scope: Admin APIs
- Out of scope: Round lifecycle transitions
- Out of scope: Git push to a remote
- Out of scope: Frontend changes
- Preserve: Existing player session handlers in backend/internal/player
- Preserve: GET /healthz


## Technical constraints
- Go 1.22, chi router, no database; persistent data lives in Git as Markdown/YAML
- Git writes go through an interface wrapping the Git CLI


## Definition of done
- All listed endpoints wired
- Unit tests with mocked Git and clock pass


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Contribution service validates prompt, world, round status, limits, rate and spam
nodes.body:
Context: no contribution logic exists. Desired behavior: Service.Submit validates prompt length, world existence, OPEN round, per-player limit of 5, request rate and duplicate/spam prompts using an injected clock. Expected result: typed errors per rule. Why: protect the Git-backed record from abuse.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a prompt shorter than MinPromptLen or longer than MaxPromptLen, when Submit runs, then ErrPromptLength is returned
- Given a world with no round source entry, when Submit runs, then ErrWorldNotFound is returned
- Given a round whose status is not OPEN, when Submit runs, then ErrRoundNotOpen is returned
- Given a player with 5 stored contributions in the round, when Submit runs, then ErrLimitReached is returned
- Given more than RateMax submissions in RateWindow by one player, when Submit runs, then ErrRateLimited is returned
- Given a prompt identical (case/whitespace-insensitive) to the player's earlier one or containing 10+ repeated identical characters, when Submit runs, then ErrDuplicate or ErrSpam is returned


## Scope
- In scope: The service rejects invalid submissions before anything is written.
- Out of scope: Admin APIs
- Out of scope: Frontend changes
- Out of scope: Git push
- Preserve: Existing player session handlers in backend/internal/player
- Preserve: GET /healthz


## Technical constraints
- Go 1.22, chi router, no database; persistent data lives in Git as Markdown/YAML
- Git writes go through an interface wrapping the Git CLI


## Definition of done
- Acceptance criteria met by implementation


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Accepted contributions are written as unique immutable Markdown files with serialized writes and sanitized paths
nodes.body:
Context: the service needs a Store. Desired behavior: Store writes worlds/<world>/rounds/<round>/contributions/<id>.md with a generated ID under a mutex, refuses overwrite, commits via the Git interface, and rejects unsafe path segments. Expected result: concurrent submissions never collide. Why: immutability and safety.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given two concurrent Save calls, when both complete, then two different files exist and each contains its own prompt
- Given an existing file for an ID, when Save would write it again, then the write fails and the file is unchanged
- Given a worldID or roundID containing .., a slash or a backslash, when Save runs, then safepath.ErrUnsafe is returned and nothing is written
- Given a saved contribution, when Get(id) and ListByPlayer run, then the stored fields are returned


## Scope
- In scope: Each contribution becomes a distinct Markdown file; traversal is rejected.
- Out of scope: Admin APIs
- Out of scope: Frontend changes
- Out of scope: Git push
- Preserve: Existing player session handlers in backend/internal/player
- Preserve: GET /healthz


## Technical constraints
- Go 1.22, chi router, no database; persistent data lives in Git as Markdown/YAML
- Git writes go through an interface wrapping the Git CLI


## Definition of done
- Acceptance criteria met by implementation


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Git writes go through an interface wrapping the Git CLI with a bot identity
nodes.body:
Context: contributions must be committed to Git. Desired behavior: gitrepo.Committer interface with a CLI implementation that runs git add and git commit with -c user.name/user.email set from the bot config via an injectable command runner. Expected result: tests mock the runner. Why: credentials never leave the backend and tests need no Git.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a CLI committer, when Commit runs, then it executes git add -- <path> then git commit with the bot name and email in the working dir
- Given the runner fails on add, when Commit runs, then commit is not executed and the error is returned
- Given an empty path list or a path with .., when Commit runs, then an error is returned and no command runs


## Scope
- In scope: A Committer interface with a CLI implementation using the configured bot identity.
- Out of scope: Admin APIs
- Out of scope: Frontend changes
- Out of scope: Git push
- Preserve: Existing player session handlers in backend/internal/player
- Preserve: GET /healthz


## Technical constraints
- Go 1.22, chi router, no database; persistent data lives in Git as Markdown/YAML
- Git writes go through an interface wrapping the Git CLI


## Definition of done
- Acceptance criteria met by implementation


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · World and current-round read endpoints serve data from the repository files
nodes.body:
Context: world data lives in worlds/<id>/world.yaml and rounds/<round>/round.yaml, game content in game/content/worlds/<id>. Desired behavior: a world repository and handlers for the four read endpoints. Expected result: JSON responses, 404 for unknown worlds. Why: the client needs world, game and round state.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given worlds/the-boys-room/world.yaml, when GET /api/v1/worlds runs, then a JSON array containing that world id is returned
- Given an unknown or unsafe world id, when GET /api/v1/worlds/{id} runs, then 404 is returned
- Given round directories, when GET /api/v1/worlds/{id}/round/current runs, then the highest-numbered round with id, number, status, starts_at and ends_at is returned
- Given game content for the world, when GET /api/v1/worlds/{id}/game runs, then the world YAML and scenes are returned as JSON


## Scope
- In scope: GET /worlds, /worlds/{id}, /worlds/{id}/game and /worlds/{id}/round/current respond from files.
- Out of scope: Admin APIs
- Out of scope: Frontend changes
- Out of scope: Git push
- Preserve: Existing player session handlers in backend/internal/player
- Preserve: GET /healthz


## Technical constraints
- Go 1.22, chi router, no database; persistent data lives in Git as Markdown/YAML
- Git writes go through an interface wrapping the Git CLI

- Acceptance criteria met by implementation

nodes.title: REQ · Contribution endpoints and world routes are wired into the server with configuration
nodes.body:
Context: server.go registers only session routes. Desired behavior: handlers for POST /api/v1/contributions, GET /api/v1/contributions/{id}, GET /api/v1/player/me/contributions identify the player from the session cookie, map service errors to HTTP statuses, and server.New wires all routes with storage and contribution limits from YAML config. Expected result: endpoints work end to end in-process. Why: expose the feature.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given no valid session cookie, when POST /api/v1/contributions runs, then 401 is returned
- Given a valid cookie and valid body {world_id, prompt}, when POST runs, then 201 with the contribution JSON is returned
- Given ErrPromptLength/ErrRoundNotOpen/ErrLimitReached/ErrRateLimited/ErrDuplicate, when POST runs, then the status is 400/409/429/429/409 respectively and ErrWorldNotFound gives 404
- Given a stored id, when GET /api/v1/contributions/{id} runs, then 200 is returned, and an unknown id gives 404
- Given a valid cookie, when GET /api/v1/player/me/contributions runs, then only that player's contributions are returned
- Given a YAML config with storage and contribution blocks, when loaded, then fields are parsed and defaults fill omitted limits


## Scope
- In scope: POST/GET contribution routes and player history are served; routes and config are wired.
- Out of scope: Admin APIs
- Out of scope: Frontend changes
- Out of scope: Git push
- Preserve: Existing player session handlers in backend/internal/player
- Preserve: GET /healthz


## Technical constraints
- Go 1.22, chi router, no database; persistent data lives in Git as Markdown/YAML
- Git writes go through an interface wrapping the Git CLI


## Definition of done
- Acceptance criteria met by implementation


## Clarifying questions
- None

steps.action: Create package contribution with errors ErrPromptLength, ErrWorldNotFound, ErrRoundNotOpen, ErrLimitReached, ErrRateLimited, ErrDuplicate, ErrSpam; type Round{ID, Status string}; interface RoundSource{Current(worldID string) (Round, error)} (returns ErrWorldNotFound for unknown world); interface Store{Save(ctx, Contribution) error; CountByPlayer(worldID, roundID, playerID string) (int, error); HasPrompt(worldID, roundID, playerID, hash string) (bool, error)}; struct Limits{MinPromptLen, MaxPromptLen, MaxPerPlayer int; RateMax int; RateWindow time.Duration}; Service{Rounds, Store, Limits, Now func() time.Time}; Submit(ctx, Input{WorldID, PlayerID, Prompt}) (Contribution, error) that trims the prompt then checks in order: length (rune count), world/round via Rounds.Current, Status == "OPEN", spam run >= 10 identical runes, rate limiter Allow(playerID, Now()), CountByPlayer >= MaxPerPlayer, HasPrompt with sha256 of lower-cased whitespace-collapsed prompt, then Store.Save.
steps.expected: Submit returns the typed error for each violated rule and calls Store.Save only when all pass

steps.action: Create rateLimiter{mu sync.Mutex; hits map[string][]time.Time; max int; window time.Duration} with Allow(key string, now time.Time) bool that drops hits older than now-window, returns false when len(hits) >= max, otherwise appends now and returns true.
steps.expected: Allow is false on the (max+1)th call within the window and true again after the window passes

nodes.title: Act: Add contribution handlers, config and route wiring
nodes.body:
Context: server.go registers only session routes. Desired behavior: handlers for POST /api/v1/contributions, GET /api/v1/contributions/{id}, GET /api/v1/player/me/contributions identify the player from the session cookie, map service errors to HTTP statuses, and server.New wires all routes with storage and contribution limits from YAML config. Expected result: endpoints work end to end in-process. Why: expose the feature.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given no valid session cookie, when POST /api/v1/contributions runs, then 401 is returned
- Given a valid cookie and valid body {world_id, prompt}, when POST runs, then 201 with the contribution JSON is returned
- Given ErrPromptLength/ErrRoundNotOpen/ErrLimitReached/ErrRateLimited/ErrDuplicate, when POST runs, then the status is 400/409/429/429/409 respectively and ErrWorldNotFound gives 404


## Scope
- In scope: POST/GET contribution routes and player history are served; routes and config are wired.
- Out of scope: Writing tests
- Out of scope: Frontend changes
- Preserve: Existing player session handlers in backend/internal/player
- Preserve: GET /healthz

- Go 1.22, chi router, no database; persistent data lives in Git as Markdown/YAML
- Git writes go through an interface wrapping the Git CLI

- Code path: `backend/internal/server/server.go`
- Code path: `backend/configs/config.example.yaml`

nodes.title: Verify: Contribution service validation unit tests
nodes.body:
Unit tests written from the requirement spec with mocked Git, clock and temp-dir filesystem only. Context: the service rejects invalid submissions before anything is written. Expected result: all listed tests pass.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a prompt shorter than MinPromptLen or longer than MaxPromptLen, when Submit runs, then ErrPromptLength is returned
- Given a world with no round source entry, when Submit runs, then ErrWorldNotFound is returned
- Given a round whose status is not OPEN, when Submit runs, then ErrRoundNotOpen is returned
- Given a player with 5 stored contributions in the round, when Submit runs, then ErrLimitReached is returned
- Given more than RateMax submissions in RateWindow by one player, when Submit runs, then ErrRateLimited is returned
- Given a prompt identical (case/whitespace-insensitive) to the player's earlier one or containing 10+ repeated identical characters, when Submit runs, then ErrDuplicate or ErrSpam is returned


## Scope
- In scope: Unit tests with fakes
- Out of scope: Running the server
- Out of scope: Browser or e2e checks
- Preserve: Existing player session handlers in backend/internal/player
- Preserve: GET /healthz

- Go 1.22, chi router, no database; persistent data lives in Git as Markdown/YAML
- Git writes go through an interface wrapping the Git CLI


## Definition of done
- Listed tests pass via the unit command

nodes.body:
Unit tests written from the requirement spec with mocked Git, clock and temp-dir filesystem only. Context: each contribution becomes a distinct Markdown file; traversal is rejected. Expected result: all listed tests pass.

- Given two concurrent Save calls, when both complete, then two different files exist and each contains its own prompt

- Given a saved contribution, when Get(id) and ListByPlayer run, then the stored fields are returned
